title: Computational neuroscience
stage: College neuroscience and cognitive science degree
audience: a college student in a neuroscience, cognitive science, psychology or biology degree program, or an adult studying the same material on their own
purpose: Learn to model neurons and networks with mathematics and simulation: integrate-and-fire neurons, the Hodgkin–Huxley model and its reductions, phase planes and excitability, synapses and short-term plasticity, recurrent networks and rate models, excitation and inhibition, attractor networks and working memory, neural coding and information, efficient coding, and network oscillations, with simulations in Python.
primary_reading: Neuronal Dynamics by Gerstner, Kistler, Naud and Paninski (free online)

weeks.4: Two-dimensional reductions and the phase plane
weeks.10: Neural coding: rates, timing and populations

blocks.deliverable: Simulate a neuron and compute its firing-rate curve.
Find the fixed points of a two-variable neuron model.
Simulate two coupled neurons with synapses.
Week 7 midterm; analyze the stability of a two-population rate model.
Simulate persistent activity in a small attractor network.
Compute the information a model neuron carries about a stimulus.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Modeling project: build and test in plain Python a small network model of one phenomenon (for example persistent activity, gain control or oscillations), explore how its behavior depends on two parameters, compare it with a simpler model, and write a short paper with the equations, tables of results and the predictions the model makes for experiments.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.

files.L04.txt: Two-dimensional reductions and the phase plane
files.L10.txt: Neural coding: rates, timing and populations
